---
title: "Filter hooks with conditions"
---

Conditions decide when a hook fires. You pass them in two lists on every
registration. `only_if` requires every condition to match. `skip_if` skips the hook
when any condition matches.

```python
from captain_hook import hook, Event, Tool, Command, RanCommand

hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    message="git stash is not allowed; use jj",
    block=True,
    only_if=[Tool("Bash"), Command(r"git\s+stash")],
    skip_if=[RanCommand(r"jj\s+shelve")],
)
```

## Combine conditions

`skip_if` runs first. If any skip condition matches, the hook is skipped and
`only_if` is never checked. So the opening hook fires when the tool is Bash **and** the
command matches `git stash`, unless the agent already ran `jj shelve`.

For an "or" inside one condition, use pipe-alternation instead of separate entries.
`Tool("Edit|Write")` matches either tool. `Tool("Edit"), Tool("Write")` requires both,
which no event satisfies.

## Pick a condition

Start from what you want to match.

| You want to match | Use |
|---|---|
| A file path | `FilePath("*.py", "*.pyi")` |
| A bash command | `Command(r"git\s+push")` |
| An edit to a source file in a language | `SourceEdits(lang="ts")` |
| A test file | `TestFile()` |
| Written or edited file content | `Content(r"print\(")` |
| The current tool | `Tool("Bash")` |
| A subagent type | `Agent("cleanup")` |
| A file edited earlier this session | `TouchedFile("**/*.py")` |
| A command run earlier this session | `RanCommand(r"uv\s+run\s+mtest")` |
| A skill used earlier this session | `UsedSkill("codex")` |
| Plan mode | `InPlanMode()` |

Most of these inspect the current event. `TouchedFile`, `RanCommand`, and
`UsedSkill` inspect the session transcript, so they tell you whether something
already happened earlier in the session. For the full table with every pattern type and default, see
[Conditions Cheatsheet](../reference/conditions.qmd).

## Match the current event

`FilePath`, `Content`, `TestFile`, and `SourceEdits` match project files only by
default. Pass `project_only=False` to target external scratch files, attachments, or
logs.

```python
from captain_hook import hook, Event, FilePath, Command, SourceEdits

# Fire only for Python files
hook(Event.PostToolUse, message="Check imports", only_if=[FilePath("*.py", "*.pyi")])

# Fire only for git push commands
hook(Event.PreToolUse, message="Run tests before pushing", block=True,
     only_if=[Command(r"git\s+push")])

# Fire only for TypeScript source edits under src/
hook(Event.PostToolUse, message="Check types", only_if=[SourceEdits(lang="ts", paths="src/**")])
```

`SourceEdits` skips test files unless you pass `include_tests=True`, so it pairs a
language with a source-only scope in one condition.

## Match the session history

Transcript conditions gate on prior actions. Use them to require a step or to skip a
hook once a step has happened.

```python
from captain_hook import hook, Event, TouchedFile, RanCommand, UsedSkill

# Fire only if Python files were edited this session
hook(Event.Stop, message="Run tests before stopping", block=True,
     only_if=[TouchedFile("**/*.py")])

# Skip the gate once the agent ran the test suite
hook(Event.Stop, message="Run tests before stopping", block=True,
     skip_if=[RanCommand(r"uv\s+run\s+mtest")])

# Fire only if the codex skill was consulted
hook(Event.Stop, message="codex was consulted", only_if=[UsedSkill("codex")])
```

## Write a custom condition

When no built-in fits, implement `CustomCondition`. It is a `runtime_checkable`
Protocol, so any frozen dataclass with a `check(self, evt) -> bool` method satisfies
it. Carry configuration as fields.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from captain_hook import CustomCondition, BaseHookEvent, hook, Event

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MinEdits(CustomCondition):
    threshold: int = 5

    def check(self, evt: BaseHookEvent) -> bool:
        return evt.ctx.t.tool_uses.where(name="Edit").count() >= self.threshold

hook(Event.Stop, message="Many edits, run a review", only_if=[MinEdits(threshold=10)])
```

Use a custom condition like any built-in in either list. The predicate goes in `check()`; the
firing goes through a primitive, never an `@on` body.

## Worked patterns

Require tests after editing source files, and skip the gate once they pass.

```python
from captain_hook import hook, Event, TouchedFile, RanCommand

hook(
    Event.Stop,
    message="Source files changed; run tests before stopping",
    block=True,
    only_if=[TouchedFile("src/**/*.py")],
    skip_if=[RanCommand(r"uv\s+run\s+mtest")],
)
```

Warn about history-rewriting commands, except during plan mode.

```python
from captain_hook import hook, Event, Tool, Command, InPlanMode

hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    message="This command modifies git history",
    block=True,
    only_if=[Tool("Bash"), Command(r"git\s+(rebase|reset|push\s+--force)")],
    skip_if=[InPlanMode()],
)
```

Lint Python files but leave test files alone.

```python
from captain_hook import hook, Event, FilePath, TestFile

hook(
    Event.PostToolUse,
    message="Check code style",
    only_if=[FilePath("*.py")],
    skip_if=[TestFile()],
)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Regex patterns"}
`Tool`, `Command`, `Content`, and `RanCommand` match with regex. Escape special
characters and use raw strings (`r"..."`) to avoid backslash issues.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Related"}
For every condition's pattern syntax and defaults, see the
[Conditions Cheatsheet](../reference/conditions.qmd). To write richer checks against
session history, see [Query the transcript](transcript.qmd).
:::
